title: Multi-value --lora-path/--lora-scale produce a LIST that crashes when fed to scalar pipeline kwargs
detail: The CLI registers --lora-scale/--lora-path as repeated/multi flags (action=append-style), so args.lora_scale / args.lora_path arrive as a Python list. Several command modules pass this list straight into a scalar kwarg: profile hands args.lora_path to pipeline.generate(lora_path=...) (expects one path), faceswap wraps args.lora_scale into lora_scales=[lora_scale] producing a nested list [[...]], expansion assigns the whole list to scalar lora_scale, workflow stuffs the list into RunConfig.lora_scale (a float dataclass field), and now video-vbvr (app/commands/video-vbvr.py, pipeline.generate call) passes args.lora_scale (list) as a scalar to LTXVideoPipeline. All are latent crashes that only fire when a user actually passes the flag along that code path — static checks miss them. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run re-flagged the SAME class leaking into VIDEO pipelines (video-relay/video-generate pass-through); 2026-06-21T17-05-15 run flagged it AGAIN in video-vbvr (scored high, type-safety dimension); the 2026-06-22T00-55 run's image-profile lora_scale falsy-coerce finding (correctness, app/commands/image-profile.py run_meta) is the list-typed-input face of the same class; the 2026-06-22T12-33 run re-flagged video-vbvr AGAIN (low, argparse-integrity-video-vbvr-364): VBVR added its OWN lora_scale list-unwrap that duplicates video-generate._first_or but SKIPS the None-scalar case — a divergent hand-rolled unwrapper per module rather than one shared helper, confirming the list-vs-scalar leak spans the WHOLE CLI surface (image AND video sub-actions) and persists across 5 runs unfixed. Fix pattern: unwrap to a scalar at the boundary (or make pipeline kwargs accept lists consistently) in BOTH image AND video paths, via ONE shared helper (not a divergent per-module copy). Found via review scan.

title: A flag's required=True is NOT satisfied by its --alias when both share the same dest
detail: refine.py registers --input-image with required=True, then app/commands/_shared registers --input to the SAME dest (input_image). argparse only recognizes the original option string for the required check, so a caller using --input (the alias) is rejected as missing-required even though the value landed in the dest. Net effect: the --input alias is permanently unusable for refine. General rule: when aliasing an option via shared dest, set required=True on only ONE registration and never rely on an alias to satisfy a required flag. Found via effort:low review-only scan (2 of 13 findings, one scored high).

title: Frame-floor helpers that early-return on a mod predicate bypass the minimum-frames guarantee
detail: video-vbvr._adjust_frames returns frames=1 unchanged when (frames-1)%8==0 — the modulo predicate is satisfied by 1 (since 0%8==0), so the 9-frame minimum is silently bypassed for that input. Pattern: any floor/ceiling helper whose guard is a divisibility/mod check rather than a direct comparison (frames < MIN) can pass the boundary value straight through. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run re-flagged the SAME class in video-relay._adjust_frames: the already-aligned branch (frames already divisible) returns frames=1 unchanged with NO min-9 clamp, identical root cause in a sibling command module; the 2026-06-22T00-55-32 run re-flagged the EXACT video-vbvr already-aligned branch (correctness-video-vbvr-200, high) a third time — confirms the mod-predicate floor bypass is a recurring cross-module pattern across 3 runs unfixed. Always express floors as explicit numeric comparisons (frames < MIN: frames = MIN), not as side-effects of a mod branch. Found via effort:low review-only scan.

title: A ternary expression used as a bare statement discards its value — correctness depends on side-effect ordering
detail: video-relay uses `x if cond else y` as a standalone statement (not assigned). The ternary evaluates only one branch and throws the result away, so any code that relied on BOTH branches' side-effects (e.g. shutil.move ordering) is fragile. Linters rarely flag it because it is syntactically valid. 2026-06-21T02-22-06 run re-flagged the SAME class in video-relay._mux_audio_track: the fallback expression-statement does nothing — the ternary in void context is confirmed dead-code-on-one-branch, not just theoretical. Rewrite as an explicit if/else so the intended branch's side-effect is unambiguous. Found via effort:low review-only scan.

title: effort:low review-only scan surfaces genuine latent bugs; adversarial-verify value depends on whether fixes are applied, not the lane tag
detail: Default cheap lane (lanes:[review,lint], fix.mode=review-only) reliably surfaces real latent bugs across runs. 2026-06-19: 13 findings, adversarialUpheld=0. 2026-06-20: 6 findings, adversarialUpheld=0. 2026-06-21T00-10: 9 findings, adversarialUpheld=0. 2026-06-21T02-22: 19 findings, adversarialUpheld=0. 2026-06-21T17-05 run (fix mode, 46 new findings, 39 verified): adversarialUpheld=6. 2026-06-22T00-55 run (review+lint, 56 new findings, 53 verified, adversarialUpheld=4, fix applied=12, regressions=0): a run TAGGED review-only that STILL applied 12 fixes with ZERO regressions and adversarialUpheld=4. 2026-06-22T00-10 run (review+lint, 50 new findings, 46 verified, adversarialUpheld=2, fix applied=12, regressions=0): confirms the zero-regression fix streak across BOTH 00-55 (12/0) and 00-10 (12/0). 2026-06-22T12-33 run (review+lint, 60 new findings, 56 verified, adversarialUpheld=1, fix applied=14, regressions=0): extends the zero-regression fix streak to THREE consecutive runs (00-55 12/0, 00-10 12/0, 12-33 14/0 = 38 fixes applied, 0 regressions), though adversarialUpheld DROPPED to 1 (from 4, then 2) — the verify gate still overturns at least one finding whenever fixes apply, so it stays load-bearing even as the overturn rate falls. Refinement holds: the discriminator for whether adversarial-verify is load-bearing is whether FIXES ARE APPLIED, NOT the lane/mode tag — a 'review-only' run that applies fixes still needs the verify gate, while a run that applies no fixes sees ~0 overturn (first 4 runs, 47 findings). Do NOT skip adversarial-verify on any run that applies fixes, regardless of its lane label. Many findings remain RE-flags of the same locus across runs (frame-floor bypass, lora list-vs-scalar, shared-flag default bleed, animate orphan) because the underlying bugs are not yet patched; the knowledge file carries stable IDs so a fix run can target them.

title: Findings cluster in command modules at the argparse->pipeline boundary; _shared.py + run_config.py are the highest-density loci; the dominant dimension rotates
detail: All findings live in app/commands/ modules where argparse args (lists, required flags, defaults) meet pipeline dataclasses (scalars, fixed kwargs) — the type-coercion/dest-collision/default-bleed seam. 2026-06-19: 13/13 in app/commands/*. 2026-06-20: 6/6 in app/commands/*. 2026-06-21T00-10: 9/9 in app/commands/*. 2026-06-21T02-22: 19 findings in app/commands/* plus _shared.py and run.py entry — _shared.py is the single highest-density locus. 2026-06-21T17-05 run (39 verified, byDimension error-handling(15)>type-safety(7)=argparse-integrity(7)=import-hygiene(7)>correctness(3)). 2026-06-22T00-55 run (56 new findings, byDimension import-hygiene(20)>type-safety(11)>error-handling(10)>argparse-integrity(9)>correctness(3)): import-hygiene was the single largest dimension. 2026-06-22T00-10 run (50 new findings, byDimension error-handling(14)=import-hygiene(14)>type-safety(9)>argparse-integrity(7)>correctness(2)). 2026-06-22T12-33 run (60 new findings, byDimension import-hygiene(28)>type-safety(12)>argparse-integrity(7)>error-handling(6)>correctness(3)): import-hygiene is the LARGEST bucket by a wide margin (28 vs next 12) — confirms import-hygiene is the modal dominant dimension across runs, with error-handling alternating. run_config.py surfaces AGAIN across runs as a recurring boundary locus (12-33 run: run_config ab_params typed dict[str,Any] but can receive list-valued JSON). Review focus on _shared.py + app/commands/* + run_config.py yields the highest bug density for this codebase. Lint lane (pyflakes/check-model/self-test) stays clean on code quality (pyflakesRealCount=0, checkModelOk=true, selftestOk=true across runs including 12-33); the lint lane is a structural-integrity backstop, not a defect finder. Note: the dominant non-correctness dimension rotates between error-handling and import-hygiene across runs — both are always present; do not tune the review prompt to favor one.

title: A hardcoded pipeline kwarg (False/None) or an omitted kwarg silently freezes/forgets a feature even if a flag exists upstream
detail: Two faces of the same trap, both in video-relay. (1) Hardcoded literal: temporal_upscale=False is passed as a literal to LTXVideoPipeline — not sourced from any arg or default; no --temporal-upscale flag is registered on the relay parser, so the code path is permanently unreachable from the relay subcommand even though the underlying pipeline and the non-relay generate path support it. (2) Omitted kwargs: relay's pipeline.generate(...) call drops audio_stage1_only, audio_cfg_scale, modality_scale, audio_path, audio_volume — the args exist upstream (the generate path threads them) but the relay copy never passes them, so relay silently runs with pipeline defaults instead of the caller's audio/modality settings. General trap: any kwarg constructed as a bare literal in a command module, OR silently dropped from a copy-pasted generate() call, decouples the feature from the CLI surface — the flag can exist (or be assumed to exist) while the behavior is frozen/forgotten. Fix: thread the value from args (default it in the defaults table, register a flag), diff the kwargs against the canonical generate path, or delete the dead capability so the frozen-False/missing-kwarg is honest. Found via effort:low review-only scan (high + medium).

title: A flag's default is duplicated across registration-order / inline magic-numbers / None-sentinels and the duplicates drift; first-writer-wins and None-sentinels poison the dest
detail: A flag's default has ONE source of truth (argparse) but is routinely DUPLICATED — in first-writer registration order, in inline literals, and in None-sentinels — and the duplicates drift. Confirmed faces: (1) first-writer-wins / shared-parser collision: image-purify registers --seed default=42 (SeedVR2 noise) while canonical t2i seed default is 777; whichever sub-action's parser builds first wins. 2026-06-21T17-05 run re-flagged the SAME class: --output is registered by BOTH purify and review on the unified image parser. (2) None-sentinel poison: image-profile registers --seed with default=None as a sentinel — because profile's parser is the FIRST/only writer on a shared dest across ALL image sub-actions on the unified parser, default=None leaks into every image sub-action's --seed. The 2026-06-22T00-55 run re-flagged the EXACT profile --seed default=None finding AGAIN (argparse-integrity-image-profile.py-153, high) — the None-sentinel persists across runs unfixed. (3) inline magic-number compare: video-generate._apply_prompt_defaults magic-number compares cfg_scale/stg_scale against the WRONG argparse defaults. Root cause unifies all three: the source-of-truth for a flag's default is argparse, but it is duplicated and the duplicates drift. The None-sentinel also enables a SIBLING falsy-coalesce bug (see gotcha:numeric-falsy-coalesce-overrides-explicit-zero) where `seed = args.seed or DEFAULT` overrides an explicit --seed 0. Fix: never re-state a default inline; resolve the value explicitly per sub-action at runtime from a fresh local (never store the sentinel in the shared dest); do not rely on registration order or on None-as-skip; register shared flags in exactly ONE place. Found via review scans.

title: Bare subprocess.run/Popen without FileNotFoundError/Timeout handling hangs or wraps a crash in an unhelpful traceback; missing-timeout is the forever-hang variant
detail: Bare subprocess calls on external binaries (ffmpeg/ffprobe/transformer-backend CLI / long-running server child) need uniform guarding. Confirmed variants. (1) video-relay._extract_last_frame calls subprocess.run([ffmpeg,...]) with capture_output=True, timeout=60 but no try/except; the SECOND call IS wrapped against TimeoutExpired but the FIRST is NOT — asymmetric guarding is the easy-to-miss form. (2) 2026-06-21T17-05 run flagged image-purify transformer-backend Popen (medium, error-handling) with NO timeout — if the child stalls the parent hangs FOREVER (worse than a traceback); and video-generate._run_caption subprocess.run (low, error-handling) lacks timeout on the broad-exception path. (3) 2026-06-22T12-33 run re-flagged the Popen variant in video-review (medium, error-handling-video-review-179): a Popen that spawns a server child leaves stdout file handle NEVER closed AND the server process NEVER reaped / NEVER given a timeout — the orphaned server + leaked fd accumulate across review runs. Pattern: any subprocess.run/Popen on a possibly-missing or possibly-stalling external binary must (a) catch FileNotFoundError and emit a guided install hint, (b) pass a timeout and catch TimeoutExpired to degrade, (c) wrap uniformly across all calls in the helper (don't guard the second and forget the first, or wrap the happy path but not the broad-exception path), and (d) for long-lived children (servers) explicitly close inherited stdout/stderr handles and reap/terminate the child on exit (communicate()+terminate()/kill() under a timeout). Missing-timeout and no-reap are the silent-forever-hang / orphan-process variants — worse than a crash because they produce no traceback to debug.

title: A handle released on the happy path (cap.release()/Image.close()) is leaked if any later line raises; try/finally / context-manager is mandatory for cv2/file/PIL handles
detail: cv2.VideoCapture/VideoWriter (and any OS handle) and PIL Image opened then released/closed only on the success path leaks the handle / leaves the file locked when any line between open and release raises. Confirmed across multiple command modules: video-segment opens VideoCapture, reads metadata, then calls cap.release() — but only on the success path. video-restore opens BOTH cv2.VideoCapture and a VideoWriter without try/finally — a later exception leaks both handles (re-flagged at the 2026-06-22T00-55 run, medium, app/commands/video-restore.py). The 2026-06-22T00-55 run ALSO added the PIL face: image-quality opens comparison images via Image.open WITHOUT a context manager, leaking the fd across the comparison-image list (low, app/commands/image-quality.py) — `with Image.open(p) as img:` is the exception-safe form. The 2026-06-22T00-10 run re-flagged the cv2 face AGAIN in video_utils (medium, error-handling-video_utils-31): OpenCV VideoCapture opened, then cap.get() called before cap.release() — if cap.get() raises on a corrupt video the handle is leaked because release is happy-path-only. General trap: a happy-path release()/close() is not resource safety. Prefer with/contextlib.closing (or try/finally) so the release is exception-safe, for cv2 handles AND PIL Image objects AND any file opened for the duration of a loop. Found via review-only scans (video-segment low 2026-06-20; video-restore medium 2026-06-21 + 2026-06-22; image-quality low 2026-06-22; video_utils medium 2026-06-22).

title: A command module that fully implements the contract (PARSER_META/add_args/run) but is absent from COMMAND_NAMES is unreachable — and can silently dispatch the WRONG model if a name shadows a live one
detail: animate.py implements PARSER_META, add_args(parser), and run(args) — the full command module contract — yet 'animate' is NOT in cli.COMMAND_NAMES nor in COMMAND_ALIASES. So build_parser never registers it. Re-flagged TWO findings in the 2026-06-21T00-10 run (a low and a medium, both naming animate.py); the 2026-06-22T00-10 run re-flagged animate.py AGAIN with TWO findings (low argparse-integrity-animate-46 + medium argparse-integrity-animate.py-7); the 2026-06-22T12-33 run escalated the SAME locus to HIGH (argparse-integrity-animate.py-1): the finding title now reads 'run.py animate silently dispatches the WRONG model' — i.e. the orphan is not merely an unknown command but actively routes to an unintended model, which is a correctness hazard (wrong output, silent), not just dead code. The orphan persists across 4 runs unfixed, confirming it was not patched. Trap: a module can pass every quality gate while being structurally unreachable (or worse, shadowing a live dispatch target). Guard: assert the module's name appears in COMMAND_NAMES (a one-line integrity test), and assert NO two registered command modules share a dispatch token, or delete the stub. The repo already has test_selftest_integrity.py for a parallel case (deleted-test references); a COMMAND_NAMES-membership assertion is the analog fix. Found via effort:low review-only scans (low 2026-06-20; low+medium 2026-06-21; low+medium 2026-06-22 00-10; HIGH 2026-06-22 12-33).

title: Help text that advertises a default the argparse default doesn't match, or a duplicate flag whose guarded twin is silently skipped, misleads users and reviewers
detail: Two related argparse-integrity gaps surfaced in the 2026-06-21T00-10 run. (1) Stale advertised default: image-t2i's help string advertises default 640/960, but the argparse default is None (the sentinel pattern) — a user reading --help is told a value is preset when it is not, and a reviewer reading help text cannot trust it as the source of truth. (2) Guarded-twin divergence: image-workflow registers --film-grain / --sharpening WITHOUT the _arg_registered guard, while image-purify registers guarded copies of the same flags — the guard dedupes and silently keeps only the FIRST (purify's) registration, so the workflow-specific help text/defaults never take effect even though they look wired. The 2026-06-22T00-10 run re-flagged the SAME class as stale COMMENT divergence (not just help text): video.py line ~115 has a comment claiming --self-test comes from add_common_generation_args() which video.py never calls (low, argparse-integrity-video.py-115), and image-purify.py has a stale guard comment claiming image-expansion registers --resolution when expansion does not, so the guard never fires for the stated reason (low, argparse-integrity-image-purify.py-85). The two are the same root cause: the comment/help/default surface and the actual argparse registration surface have drifted apart, and nothing asserts they agree. Fix: treat help text AND comments as a contract — add an integrity test that parses --help and asserts each flag's advertised default equals argparse's actual default; grep comments referencing functions to confirm the call exists; and for shared flags, register in exactly ONE place (canonical t2i/_shared) and never re-add unguarded in a sub-action. Found via effort:low review-only scans (image-t2i low, image-workflow low 2026-06-21; video.py + image-purify.py 2026-06-22).

title: _arg_registered / _option_registered use parser._actions (a private argparse attribute) to detect prior registration — fragile across argparse versions
detail: app/commands/_shared._arg_registered and _option_registered check whether a flag is already registered by scanning parser._actions for matching option strings. parser._actions is an undocumented private attribute of argparse.ArgumentParser; its shape/contents are not part of the stable API and can change across Python versions or argparse refactors. A registration-guard built on a private attribute can silently mis-detect (false-negative -> duplicate-add crash; false-positive -> flag skipped) after a stdlib upgrade. Re-flagged at the 2026-06-22T00-55 run (low, argparse-integrity, app/commands/_shared.py _arg_registered / _option_registered locus) — confirms the private-attribute dependency persists. The robust check uses only documented behavior: wrap add_argument in try/except argparse.ArgumentError (the documented signal that an option string is already taken), or maintain an explicit set of registered dest/option-strings in the helper. Prefer the try/except-ArgumentError pattern — it relies only on argparse's documented behavior and needs no private-attribute access. Found via effort:low review-only scans (medium 2026-06-21T02-22; low 2026-06-22).

title: sys.path.insert(0, ...) in the entry module (run.py) matches the known KB 'sys.path.insert(0) in library modules' anti-pattern (milder in an entry module)
detail: run.py (the CLI entry point) calls sys.path.insert(0, ...) to make app/ importable. This matches the repo's existing KB guidance against sys.path.insert(0) manipulation. In an ENTRY module the risk is lower than in a library module (there is no caller whose sys.path gets polluted before its own imports), but the pattern still couples importability to CWD/launch path and hides the real packaging fix (a proper package install / pyproject.toml / console_scripts entry point). Prefer declaring the project as an installable package so run.py is reached via a console_script and app/ is importable without path mutation. Keep this distinct from the library-module variant (which is strictly worse because it poisons every importer). Found via effort:low review-only scan (low, run.py entry).

title: A loop body that reads args.* / shared dicts for every iteration aliases shared state across iterations instead of per-iteration copies
detail: Per-iteration loops that read shared argparse args or shared dicts alias state across iterations: if any iteration (or the called pipeline) mutates the object in place (append to a list field, set an attribute, cache by identity), subsequent iterations see the mutated state — cross-variant contamination invisible when each variant is independent but catastrophic if a frame/image is cached by identity. Confirmed loci: video-generate's A/B variation generate() uses args.input_image / args.audio for ALL variants (medium 2026-06-21T02-22). 2026-06-21T17-05 run re-flagged the SAME class in TWO new loci: video-relay variant loop mutates shared args object (copy.copy is a SHALLOW copy — nested dicts/lists still alias; medium, correctness, video-relay), and run_config.py ab_params is typed as dict but shared across A/B variations without deep copy (medium, correctness, run_config). The 2026-06-22T00-55 run re-flagged the run_config.py ab_params locus AGAIN (low, type-safety, app/run_config.py — ab_params field read from args.ab_params_json transient attr without fallback typing). The 2026-06-22T12-33 run re-flagged the class TWICE more: (a) video-generate FLF2V A/B variation loop ignores var_args.end_image resolution and reuses the shared begin/end paths for every variant (medium, correctness-video-generate-491) — the per-variant override is silently dropped, so every variant runs against the SAME begin/end images; (b) run_config.py ab_params typed dict[str,Any] but _resolve_ab_params can receive list-valued JSON (low, type-safety-run-config-132) — the typed-dict surface does not constrain the JSON shape, so a list slips through the shared-state seam. Confirms the trap spans video-relay + run_config + video-generate (FLF2V + A/B) — shallow copy.copy is NOT enough and the typed-dict annotation gives false safety; need copy.deepcopy for nested structures AND schema validation at the resolve boundary. Fix: deep-copy or freshly resolve per-iteration inputs at the top of each loop body (copy.deepcopy(args.input_image) / re-read from source), validate JSON shape before storing into a typed field, and never assume args.* or a shared dict is immutable across iterations. Static analysis rarely catches this because the read looks read-only. Found via review scans.

title: ffmpeg -sseof -N (seek-from-end) fails or mis-extracts on segments shorter than N seconds
detail: video-relay._extract_last_frame invokes ffmpeg with -sseof -3 (seek 3s before end-of-file) to grab the last frame. On segments shorter than 3s the -sseof offset lands before the start and ffmpeg either errors or extracts the wrong frame, silently breaking last-frame extraction for short clips. Pattern: any ffmpeg seek-from-end (-sseof) or duration-dependent flag must clamp the offset to the actual media duration (probe with ffprobe first, or compute min(offset, duration)). Do NOT assume a fixed -sseof offset is valid for all inputs — short segments are the edge case that breaks it. Fix: ffprobe the duration, clamp the seek offset, and fall back to extracting the final frame by index when the segment is shorter than the offset. Found via review scan (medium, correctness, video-relay._extract_last_frame).

title: `value or DEFAULT` falsy-coalesces explicit 0/0.0/empty into DEFAULT — silent override for numeric args where 0 is valid
detail: Reading a numeric arg as `x = args.x or DEFAULT` treats an EXPLICIT user-supplied 0 (or 0.0, or empty string) as 'unset' and silently substitutes DEFAULT — the caller's explicit value is lost with no error. This is the runtime-side twin of the default=None sentinel poison (gotcha:argparse-shared-flag-default-bleeds-first-writer-wins): the sentinel makes None mean 'unset', and the falsy-coalesce makes 0 mean 'unset', so BOTH None and 0 are mis-read. Confirmed loci: 2026-06-22T00-55 run — image-quality seed handling `seed = args.seed or DEFAULT` overrides an explicit --seed 0 (medium, correctness, app/commands/image-quality.py); image-profile run_meta lora_scale falsy-coerce overrides an explicit 0.0 (medium, correctness, app/commands/image-profile.py — list-typed input makes it doubly wrong, intersecting gotcha:lora-multi-flag-list-vs-scalar). 2026-06-22T00-10 run re-flagged the SAME class in video-t2i2v (medium, correctness-video-t2i2v-71): an `or` pattern overrides an explicit --seed 0 to 99 — now confirmed across BOTH image-quality/image-profile AND video-t2i2v, spanning image and video sub-commands. Fix: always use identity-unset semantics `x if x is not None else DEFAULT` for numeric args where 0/0.0 is a valid explicit value; NEVER use truthiness (`or`) as the 'was it provided' test for numbers. The falsy-coalesce class is distinct from the None-sentinel registration trap but the two co-occur and amplify each other — the sentinel leaks None, the coalesce treats both None and 0 as unset. Found via effort:low review-only scans.

title: Pipeline events left embedded in the timings dict are lost to callers and pollute the timing record
detail: video-generate._run_single (app/commands/video-generate.py, correctness-video-generate-891, high) captures LTX pipeline timing into a timings dict but never LIFTS the LTX events out of that dict — the events stay embedded inside the timings record, so (a) event consumers never see them (events are effectively lost), and (b) the timings dict is polluted with event data that should live in a separate events structure. General trap: when a helper returns a composite dict carrying BOTH timings AND structured events, failing to destructure/lift the events at the boundary means every downstream consumer that reads timings gets corrupted metrics, and every event consumer gets nothing. Fix: explicitly extract events into their own field/return-value at the boundary (events = timings.pop('events', []) or a separate return slot), and assert in a test that timings contains no event keys. Distinct from gotcha:loop-shared-args-state-mutation (which is cross-iteration aliasing) — this is a single-return-value destructuring omission. Found via effort:low review-only scan (high, correctness, video-generate).

title: A context-manager __enter__ / lock-acquire except clause that catches too broadly (BaseException OR plain Exception) masks unexpected acquisition errors or swallows control-flow signals
detail: A lock/context-manager __enter__ that catches broadly 'to clean up on any failure' over-catches. Two confirmed faces. (1) BaseException: video-generate GpuLock.__enter__ (app/commands/video-generate.py, correctness-video-generate-410 / error-handling, low) wraps the acquire in an except clause catching BaseException subclasses broader than intended — catching BaseException (or bare except, which in py3 catches BaseException) swallows KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, and GeneratorExit, preventing clean Ctrl-C / interpreter-shutdown / generator-teardown signals from propagating. (2) Plain Exception: gpu_monitor.py GpuLock.__enter__ (app/gpu_monitor.py, error-handling-gpu-monitor-431, low) catches Exception — less severe than BaseException but STILL risks masking unexpected acquisition errors (e.g. a real lock-corruption / flock-EBADF) as a benign 'failed to acquire' retry. The 2026-06-22T12-33 run confirms the over-catch is now in TWO modules (video-generate + gpu_monitor), both GpuLock.__enter__ — the same lock-acquire cleanup pattern duplicated across modules with the same over-broad catch. Fix: inside __enter__ catch only the SPECIFIC expected failure (e.g. TimeoutError for a timed acquire, or the documented lock-busy error), NOT Exception and NOT BaseException; if cleanup must run on control-flow exceptions, put it in __exit__ where it runs via the documented context-manager protocol rather than a broad except. Bare `except:` is equivalent to `except BaseException:` in py3 — always name the exception class you intend. Found via effort:low review-only scans (low BaseException 2026-06-22 00-10; low Exception 2026-06-22 12-33).

title: One metric aliased to another (motion_mean = flicker_mean) makes a 'has X' gate fire on the wrong signal — it never fires independently
detail: video-t2i2v (app/commands/video-t2i2v.py, correctness-video-t2i2v-300, medium): motion_mean is computed as an ALIAS of flicker_mean (same value / same source), so a downstream 'has motion' gate that is supposed to branch on motion strength is actually branching on flicker — the motion gate never fires independently of flicker. The bug is invisible to a reader because both names look like distinct metrics, and a test that exercises the gate under a motion-only / flicker-only scenario is the only thing that exposes it. General trap: when two metrics share a name relationship (alias, copy, or one derived purely from the other without an independent signal), any gate predicated on the aliased metric is really predicated on its source — the semantic the gate advertises (motion) is not the semantic it evaluates (flicker). Fix: give each metric an independent computation/source, OR rename the gate to match what it actually tests (has_flicker), OR delete the dead alias; add a test that drives the aliased metric with motion-only input (flicker held constant) and asserts the gate responds. Distinct from gotcha:events-left-in-timings-dict (data lost) — here the metric exists but carries the wrong signal. Found via effort:low review-only scan (medium, correctness, video-t2i2v).

title: A pad-list helper that repeats the LAST element silently injects a duplicate frame/scale where a neutral default (1.0 / copy-last-frame) is expected
detail: video-generate._scale_list (app/commands/video-generate.py, correctness-video-generate-413, low): when padding a list of per-frame scales to the frame count, the helper REPEATS THE LAST SCALE for the missing slots instead of defaulting to a neutral 1.0 (no-scale). Net effect: trailing frames get the last specified scale applied even though the caller intended 'no further scaling past the end' — a silent semantic shift where the pad value is data-derived (the last input) rather than a neutral identity. The bug is easy to miss because repeating-the-last is a common pad idiom and only looks wrong when the last scale is far from 1.0. General trap: padding a sequence with a DATA-DERIVED value (repeat-last, repeat-first) rather than a NEUTRAL/IDENTITY default (1.0 for scales, 0.0 for offsets, a copy of the last frame for frame-padding) silently changes the meaning of the padded region — the padded tail behaves like the last input, not like the identity. Fix: pad with the semantically-neutral default for the quantity (1.0 for multiplicative scales, or document + assert that repeat-last is intended); add a test that pads a list ending in a non-1.0 scale and asserts the padded slots equal the neutral default. Found via effort:low review-only scan (low, correctness, video-generate).
